mission: AIPI runs regular polls of US voters (often with YouGov) and publishes research on advanced AI, to show policymakers and journalists what the public thinks about AI risk and which policies it supports.

key_work.title: First AIPI poll (July 2023)
key_work.plain_summary: YouGov poll of 1,001 US voters: 83% think AI could accidentally cause a catastrophic event, 72% want to slow AI down, and 82% don't trust tech executives to self-regulate.

key_work.title: Voters oppose open-sourcing powerful models (Sept 2023 poll)
key_work.plain_summary: Found voters opposed open-sourcing powerful AI models by about 2:1 and supported a government seat on AI-company boards.

key_work.title: Voters prefer mandated safety over self-regulation (2024 poll)
key_work.plain_summary: 80% of voters preferred rules mandating safety measures for the most advanced AI over letting companies regulate themselves.

status_note: founded May 2023, public launch Aug 2023; sister advocacy group AI Policy Network (also led by Daniel Colson)
status_raw: active — founded May 2023, public launch Aug 2023; sister advocacy group AI Policy Network (also led by Daniel Colson)

warnings.text: AI capability growth is outpacing our understanding of these systems' behaviour and risks.
Most voters believe AI could accidentally cause a catastrophic event.
Voters do not trust AI executives to regulate themselves.

recommendations.text: Ground AI governance in public opinion and evidence.
Adopt oversight such as compute infrastructure oversight and pre-deployment safety evaluation.
Slow the pace of frontier AI development (reflecting majority voter preference in AIPI polls).
